sermon.title: Why is the U.S. Church Mocked and Rejected?
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Why Is the U.S. Church Mocked and Rejected?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews America’s four great spiritual awakenings and says the church fell asleep while the enemy sowed tares. He says Christians invite mockery by speech that sounds insane and by behavior no different from the world, including fighting over doctrines that hurt no one. His answer is to stop shunning those who disagree, live by the two commandments of love, do good, and respond with love.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the captions give “the evolution of slavery,” read here as the abolition of slavery, and “pre and pro-civil war,” read as pre- and post-Civil War; a test he names is garbled in the captions and shown as [unclear]. He names “Matthew 22:40” for loving God (the commandments are in Matthew 22:37-40), cites Galatians 5:20 for a list that runs through Galatians 5:19-21, and quotes Jesus’ “sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon you” (John 5:14) without naming it. He says “In God We Trust” was put on money in 1954 and “under God” in the pledge in 1956; published sources give 1954 for the pledge and 1956-57 for the motto. He names authors who predicted Christ’s return (LaHaye and “Smith of Calvary Chapel”), and he criticizes teachings such as once saved always saved, faith-only prosperity and healing without doctors, date-setting, tongues without interpretation, and false healings; these are his own views and are kept as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What were America’s great spiritual awakenings?
chunks.short_answer: He asks why the U.S. church is mocked and rejected and says history records four great awakenings, the first in 1730 before the Revolutionary War and the second from 1800 to 1840, which addressed alcohol, tobacco, slavery and women’s rights.
chunks.text: And we thank you and appreciate you joining us in further pursuit of clarity on crucial choices. Today we’re going to ask the question: has the United States of America church made the best choices? Or, why is the United States church mocked and rejected today? Now, we know from history there have been four great spiritual awakenings. The first was in 1730, preceding the Revolutionary War and preparing us for it. The second was in 1800 through 1840, where alcohol, tobacco, the abolition of slavery and women’s rights was addressed.

chunks.section_question: Why does the church keep needing revival?
chunks.short_answer: He describes the third and fourth awakenings and says that when you go to sleep you have to be reawakened. From Matthew 13:25 he says that while men slept the enemy sowed tares among the wheat, and that is what happens when the church goes to sleep.
chunks.text: The third one was 1850 through the 1900s, and pre- and post-Civil War, and they address the social ills of the drunks, the orphans, the widows and so forth. The fourth was in 1948 through ‘80, where the Holy Spirit was poured out, miracles happened, praise and worship was introduced to the church, unity. And in the, the secular world, In God We Trust was put on our money in 1954, and One Nation Under God was put in our pledge in 1956, and throughout the ‘50s millions of Americans made a decision to serve Jesus Christ. Now, why do we need four awakenings? Well, when you go to sleep, you have to be reawakened, either by yourself naturally or an alarm. In Matthew 13:25 Jesus said, while men slept, his enemies came and sowed tares among the wheat. So the children of the wicked one, the children of Satan, among the wheat, while men slept. And so that’s what happens when the church goes to sleep: we need an awakening. In the ‘60s, Bible, prayer and Jesus was put out of public places and public schools; the sexual revolution and evolution was replacing them.

chunks.section_question: Why do people think Christians are crazy?
chunks.short_answer: He traces what replaced the Bible in each decade since the 1960s and says the gap between awakenings has been 10, 30 and 50 years. He says Christians talk “like they’re crazy,” citing 1 Corinthians 14:9 and 14:23.
chunks.text: In the ‘70s, abortion, drugs, homosexual agenda and rock and roll was the main focus of America. In the ‘80s, corrupt activist leaders fighting against these evils, and corrupt ministers and priests were exposed; many gave up the fight and left the enemy seeds to grow by themselves. In the ‘90s, psychology, grace and faith, entertainment, seeker-friendly church, intellectual reasoning replaced the Holy Spirit’s power and the power of the Bible. It took between the previous awakenings was 10, 30 and 50 years. There is 30 years between the last awakening and the one we are looking for. Now, what are the reasons for mockery and rejection of Christians? Christians talk like crazy, like they’re crazy. First Corinthians 14:9: unless you utter by the tongue words easy to understand. Verse 23: they will, will they not say that you are out of your mind? You are, you people are nuts.

chunks.short_answer: From 1 Peter 4:14 he says you are blessed if insulted for the name of Christ, but not if insulted as an evildoer. He says “once saved, always saved” is insane talk, because you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.
chunks.text: In First Peter 4:14, if you’re insulted because of the name of Christ, you are blessed, and happy are you. But if you’re insulted as an evildoer, you are not blessed. And so our behavior and our speech invite mockery and rejection and insults. Eternal salvation: here’s some, a list of some insane Christian speech. Once saved, always saved from sin, sin’s penalty, that they have wrath, and Satan. That’s like saying the blind man and the leper and all them that got healed from their diseases would never have to be delivered from sickness again, when Jesus said, go and sin no more, lest something worse come upon you. You don’t get something for nothing; you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.

chunks.text: And so we’re going to look into why Christians are insulted and mocked because of their behavior. Sectarian issues that we divide over that directly hurt no one, like water baptism, tongues, worship, second coming, anointing or holy water, women in the ministry, hair, clothing, jewelry and so forth. They hurt nobody. Why in the world do we fight and argue over things that don’t physically or financially, mentally hurt anybody? And the humanists look at us and go, man, you guys are a bunch of crackpots, all of you are saying the different things. And so they insult us and they mock us, and we invite it in our behavior. And yet we say we got eternal life and they’re going to the lake of fire, and so the people outside of the church go, that’s insane, that’s nuts, you’re no different than I am.

chunks.section_question: What two commandments sum up the Bible?
chunks.short_answer: He says to stop shunning those who disagree with our petty doctrines, because the whole Bible hangs on two commandments: love God, and love your neighbor as yourself. He adds Romans 13 (love does no harm) and Matthew 7:12 (treat others as you would have them treat you).
chunks.text: So let’s stop mistreating and shunning those that disagree with our petty little doctrines. We got more important things to work on. The Bible now is summed up in two doctrines. The Bible says on these two doctrines hang all the law and the prophets, the whole book. Another scripture says it is the law and the prophets. And these two doctrines summarize the Bible, and humanists are wrong when they say the Bible is a bunch of lies, because there’s nothing wrong with these two doctrines. First one is to love God, Matthew 22:40. And Romans 13 tells us that love does no harm to his neighbor, therefore love fulfills the law, and everyone has to agree we should not be harming each other, whether you’re a humanist, an atheist or a Christian. That is a good law, and that sums up the Bible. The next one is love your neighbor as yourself, that’s the second one. And to clarify it, he says in Matthew 7:12, treat others as you would have them treat you.

First Corinthians 13 clarifies love: patience; love is kind; it’s not envious; it’s not rude; it’s not proud; it doesn’t brag about itself; doesn’t promote evil; doesn’t think evil; is not eagerly angered, easily angered; and it doesn’t demand its own way. And the conclusion is this: we need as Christians to speak and behave in a manner that doesn’t invite these things, and respond with love to love violators. That’s the way of our Creator.
